The two-token-store split (confirmed by `LEGACY_QB_REPLACEMENT` messaging and `ENABLE_LEGACY_USER_SCOPED_QB_SYNC` flag in routes-quickbooks.ts) is a known-in-progress migration, but `quickbooks-sync.ts` layers the new gate on top of the old token flow without reconciling them.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) make these functions actually consume the `QbConnection` row returned by `findActive()` to build the QB client, fully migrating off `userIntegrations`, or (b) if superseded by `qbInvoiceSyncService`/`qbPaymentSyncService` (referenced in routes-quickbooks.ts as the new path), delete the unused `findActive()` call and clearly mark `quickbooks-sync.ts` as legacy-only.

findings.title: Process-local in-memory state (customerCache, recentErrors, lastSyncTime) is unsafe on serverless/multi-instance deployment
findings.detail: `customerCache` (line 88), `lastSyncTime` (line 92), and `recentErrors` (lines 93-98) are module-level variables holding process-local state, used by `findOrCreateQBCustomer`, `syncInvoiceToQuickBooks`, `syncPaymentToQuickBooks`, and surfaced via `getSyncStatus()` (used by `/quickbooks/sync/status`).
findings.impact: On Vercel/serverless, each invocation may run in a different or freshly cold-started context, so `customerCache` provides no reliable cross-request benefit and can serve a stale QB customer ID after a customer merge/dedup in QBO. `lastSyncTime`/`recentErrors` reported by the sync dashboard are inconsistent per-instance and lose all history on cold start — exactly what the newer `qb_sync_log` table with its `/quickbooks/diagnostics` endpoint was built to replace.
findings.recommendation: If `quickbooks-sync.ts` remains active, replace `customerCache` with a persisted lookup (e.g. `qb_entity_map` keyed by `atosEntityType='customer'`) and replace `recentErrors`/`lastSyncTime` with a query against `qb_sync_log`.

findings.title: Legacy QuickBooks OAuth flow is gated by a single global env var with no per-tenant scoping, and defaults enabled in test env
findings.detail: `legacyUserScopedQuickBooksEnabled()` (src/server/routes/routes-quickbooks.ts:117-123) gates the entire legacy OAuth/callback/sync/disconnect flow behind one process-wide `ENABLE_LEGACY_USER_SCOPED_QB_SYNC` env var for all schools and users simultaneously; there is no per-school migration flag, and the flag defaults true in `NODE_ENV === 'test'`.
findings.impact: Low likelihood but non-trivial blast radius: an accidental flip of this single flag in production re-opens `/quickbooks/auth-url`, `/quickbooks/callback`, `/quickbooks/sync/*` for all tenants at once, potentially creating `userIntegrations` rows that diverge from the intended `qb_connections`/`accounting_provider_connections` system of record, and re-exposes the invoiceUrl-discard and query-escaping bugs above.
findings.recommendation: Once the migration off the legacy path is confirmed complete, remove the legacy routes/flag entirely rather than leaving a global kill-switch that can silently reactivate a superseded subsystem.

findings.title: Schema comment documents a 4-part encrypted-token format that neither decrypt() implementation in this slice matches
findings.detail: `src/lib/schema/quickbooks.ts:40` documents the `qb_connections` encrypted token format as `${iv}:${tag}:${data}:${version}` (4 parts including a version segment). Both `decrypt()` implementations in this slice (`src/lib/quickbooks.ts:46-55` and `src/server/routes/routes-quickbooks.ts:78-87`) destructure only 3 parts with no version field, and their paired `encrypt()` functions only ever produce 3-part strings.
findings.impact: Low direct impact since the 3-part functions are internally self-consistent, but the stale 4-part comment on the `qb_connections` table (written to by out-of-slice token-service code, not these two files) could mislead a future developer implementing key-rotation/version-aware decryption, or mask that the two parallel QB token stores use different encryption code paths that happen to currently produce the same 3-part shape.
findings.recommendation: Verify against the out-of-slice `qbTokenService.ts` whether a 4-part format is actually produced there; if not, fix the comment in `src/lib/schema/quickbooks.ts` to match reality.

findings.title: Owned-path scan target src/app/api/quickbooks-callback does not exist in the repository
findings.detail: The scan mandate lists `src/app/api/quickbooks-callback` as an owned path, but no such directory exists. The actual QB OAuth callback lives at `src/app/api/integrations/qbo/callback/route.ts` (part of the newer `accounting_provider_connections`-based integration, outside this slice's literal file list), and the frontend callback landing page is `src/components/features/mvp-v2/pages/quickbooks-callback.tsx`. The legacy callback logic lives inline in `src/server/routes/routes-quickbooks.ts` (`POST /quickbooks/callback`, already reviewed).
findings.impact: Not a code defect — flagging so the scan orchestrator can correct the slice's owned-path list; nothing was left unscanned because nothing exists at the listed path.
findings.recommendation: Update the scan configuration to point at `src/app/api/integrations/qbo/callback/route.ts` and `src/components/features/mvp-v2/pages/quickbooks-callback.tsx` if they should be covered by this or another slice.
